data.title: Look-Alike Domains Registered Against the Brand
data.summary: Domains closely resembling the organisation's own were registered by third parties. Whether or not they are in use today, they are the infrastructure a phishing or invoice-fraud campaign against this organisation would run from.
data.description:
Look-alike registration is cheap and unregulated. Character substitution, hyphenation, an added word, an alternative top-level domain, and homoglyphs from other scripts all produce a name that survives a glance at the address bar.

The value to an attacker is credibility. Mail from such a domain passes the checks a recipient performs by eye, and can be given its own valid certificate and authentication records, so it passes the technical checks too — the domain is legitimately theirs.

Supplier look-alikes matter as much as your own: invoice fraud usually arrives from a near-miss of the supplier's domain rather than of the client's.
data.recommendation:
* Monitor new registrations and certificate transparency for names resembling yours and your significant suppliers'.
* Defensively register the obvious variants, and the top-level domains your customers would assume.
* Publish strict SPF, DKIM and DMARC with enforcement, so spoofing your real domain is hard and attackers are pushed to look-alikes you are watching.
* Take down what is actively used, and keep a record of the rest.
data.short_recommendation: Monitor registrations and certificate transparency for near-miss domains.
